text: Collect user and public-interest evidence for the Prototype Fund application
description: Interview at least five open-source maintainers, agent-tool developers, or small technical teams. Test the problem statement: intent and dependencies drift away from code; agent work is difficult to inspect; issue trackers capture tasks but not value/rationale. Capture concrete quotes only with permission, current workflows, failed alternatives, desired integrations, and willingness to test the prototype. Seek 2-3 lightweight letters or written commitments to pilot.

reflections.context: The Prototype Fund draft identified external user evidence as its weakest point, while actual outreach and interviews require Felix's relationships and consent.
reflections.outcome: Prepared meta/applications/prototype-fund-2026/user-research-kit.md and user-research-tracker.csv: a neutral invitation, 11 event-focused interview questions, separate consent prompts, evidence-strength rubric, negative-evidence rule, synthesis protocol, five blank participant rows, and a non-binding pilot commitment template.
reflections.effectiveness: Preparation friction is removed without fabricating interviews, quotes, demand, or pilot commitments. The tracker has 18 consistent columns and git diff --check passes.
reflections.lesson: The autonomous loop can prepare the institutional interface, but externally valid evidence begins only when a real person agrees, speaks, and grants the relevant permissions.

status.comment: Requires Felix outreach and interviews; the agent can prepare scripts and synthesize notes.
